subject: anatomy
title: Thoracic wall, intercostal spaces and diaphragm

steps.tx: The thoracic wall is a **bony cage** of ribs, sternum and thoracic vertebrae, layered with intercostal muscles. Ribs are classed as typical (3rd to 9th) or atypical (1st, 2nd, 10th, 11th, 12th). By sternal attachment, ribs 1 to 7 are **true ribs**, while 8 to 12 are false ribs. Ribs 8 to 10 are vertebrochondral and 11 and 12 are floating. Exam questions often ask which rib is false or which rib is atypical, so learn these groups cleanly.
steps.say: The thoracic wall is a bony cage made of ribs, the sternum and thoracic vertebrae, layered with intercostal muscles. Ribs are classed as typical, from the 3rd to the 9th, or atypical, which are the 1st, 2nd, 10th, 11th and 12th. By sternal attachment, ribs 1 to 7 are true ribs, while 8 to 12 are false ribs. Ribs 8 to 10 are vertebrochondral and 11 and 12 are floating.

steps.tx: Each intercostal space contains a **neurovascular bundle** sitting in the costal groove on the lower border of the rib above. From top to bottom the order is **vein, artery, nerve**. Therefore, a needle for **thoracocentesis** should enter along the upper border of the rib below, keeping clear of the bundle. The **internal thoracic artery** runs just lateral to the sternum and gives anterior intercostal branches to the upper six spaces.

steps.tx: The diaphragm has three large openings. The **caval opening** at T8 transmits the inferior vena cava and right phrenic nerve branches. The **oesophageal hiatus** at T10 transmits the oesophagus and vagal trunks. The **aortic hiatus** at T12 is behind the diaphragm, transmitting the aorta, thoracic duct and azygos vein. Remember the thoracic thread: the number of letters in vena cava (8), oesophagus (10) and aortic hiatus (12) gives the level.
steps.say: The diaphragm has three large openings. The caval opening at T8 transmits the inferior vena cava and branches of the right phrenic nerve. The oesophageal hiatus at T10 transmits the oesophagus and vagal trunks. The aortic hiatus at T12 lies behind the diaphragm and transmits the aorta, thoracic duct and azygos vein. Remember the letter count: vena cava has 8 letters, oesophagus 10, and aortic hiatus 12.

steps.tx: The diaphragm is supplied motorly by the **phrenic nerve** (C3, C4, C5), which keeps it alive: C3, 4 and 5 keep the diaphragm alive. Its central part has sensory fibres from the phrenic nerve, while the periphery is supplied by the lower six intercostal nerves. Because of this, irritated diaphragmatic peritoneum can refer pain to the shoulder. The right dome sits higher than the left, supported by the liver, and the right crus has a sphincteric action on the oesophagus.
steps.say: The diaphragm receives its motor supply from the phrenic nerve, arising from C3, C4 and C5. Its central part has sensory fibres from the phrenic nerve, while the periphery is supplied by the lower six intercostal nerves. Irritated diaphragmatic peritoneum can refer pain to the shoulder. The right dome sits higher than the left, supported by the liver, and the right crus has a sphincteric action on the oesophagus.
